participants.name: German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR)

events.use_of_proceeds: Stellarator hub coordinated with Proxima Fusion and Max Planck IPP; Gauss share undisclosed (hub round total about EUR 125M across three hubs, not attributed to Gauss)

notes: Little evidenced. Gauss Fusion is an industry-consortium GmbH (founders Alcen, ASG Superconductors, Bruker EAS, IDOM, RI Research Instruments); the only funding amount found in a robots-permitted primary source is the EUR 8M founders' pre-seed (Feb 2023, Bruker release). The census lists a "Grant 2024-04" and "EUR17M known" with no archivable source found in this pass; not recorded. The Bruker release does not give per-founder amounts or say which founders put in the EUR 8M, so the five founding companies are listed as participants on the strength of "founders' pre-seed financing" (reviewer: confirm). BMFTR Fusion Hub STRIDE (coordinated by Proxima Fusion, Gauss Fusion and Max Planck IPP) is funded from a EUR 125M first round across three hubs; Gauss's share is undisclosed so no amount is recorded. Not found in CORDIS (no HE/H2020 hits per probe); no Foerderkatalog access (403); no Gauss-specific EIB/EIC record found. WebSearch budget exhausted. Verifier: the STRIDE announced_on evidence quoted the coordinator sentence, which carries no date; replaced with the BMFTR page date ("Meldung 29.07.2026") and kept the coordinator sentence as recipient evidence. The page says the three hubs will "soon" connect and BMFTR provides "initially" EUR 125M across them, so Gauss's share is unknown and may not yet be obligated. Founders' pre-seed participants: the release lists the five founding companies but does not state that each contributed to the EUR 8M; kept on the strength of "founders' pre-seed", residual doubt.
